say: Some animals just refuse to grow old. Here are five creatures that are basically immortal, or pretty darn close.
Number one: the naked mole rat. A rodent this tiny should live about six years. These wrinkly little guys can pass thirty.
Even weirder, their risk of dying doesn't go up as they get older. For a mammal, that's basically unheard of.
Number two: Ming the clam. Scientists counted the growth rings on its shell and found it was five hundred and seven years old.
The catch? Ming got frozen with about two hundred other clams before anyone knew how old it was. Oops.
Number three: the Greenland shark. Scientists dated the lenses in their eyes, and the biggest one was about three hundred ninety two years old.
Number four: the hydra. It swaps out its cells about every four weeks, so its risk of dying never goes up with age.
And number five, the weirdest: the immortal jellyfish. When it gets hurt or stressed, it turns back into a baby polyp and starts life over.
But none of them are truly unbeatable. Predators, disease and accidents still get them. Immortal, just not invincible.
Which one would you want to be? Follow Simply Weird for more weird stuff like this.
